picks.why: The Keuka Lake house founded in 1962 as Vinifera Wine Cellars by a Ukrainian born plant scientist who showed that grafted vinifera could live through Finger Lakes winters; its Dry Riesling is the bottle that carried that argument.
picks.note: Confirm the founding as Vinifera Wine Cellars in 1962 from the house and a second source, and the Dry Riesling's sources of fruit for the years taught. The Rkatsiteli and the Chateau Frank sparkling wines go in others. Name the founder only with his dates from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Seneca Lake estate founded at Dundee in 1979 by a Mosel born grower, whose nursery grafted vines for growers across the East; the HJW Vineyard Riesling, the single vineyard wine that carries the founder's initials, is the house's Riesling to know.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 1979 (the library's), the HJW Vineyard's place and the wine's style by vintage (dry or with a little sweetness) from the house and a second source; the Dry Riesling and the Magdalena Vineyard Riesling go in others. Whether the founder is living is not settled here: name him only if two sources give his death with its date, else say the founder.

picks.why: A Keuka Lake house making Riesling and Cabernet Franc in a dry, restrained style from Keuka and Seneca fruit; the Argetsinger Vineyard Dry Riesling, from one of the old vineyards of Seneca Lake, on limestone, is the one to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year (2000 or 2001 by different accounts) and the Argetsinger Vineyard's shore, age and soils from the house and a second source; one review alone was read here for the site. Name no living person: say the founding couple.

picks.why: A vineyard on the east shore of Seneca Lake given almost wholly to Riesling and bottled by clone and by sweetness; No. 239 Dry Riesling is a single clone wine of Geisenheim clone 239, a lesson in what a clone brings to a glass.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the planting year and the vineyard's place from the house. The wines have been made at other Seneca Lake wineries, by different accounts at different houses in different years: teach the vineyard as the house and name no cellar as its maker without two sources. Name no living person.

picks.why: A Seneca Lake house founded with a partner from the southern Rhône, making bone dry Riesling and Pinot Noir in a European idiom; the Classique Dry Riesling, blended from sites on the east shore of the lake, is its wine to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year (2011 by most accounts) and the partners from the house and a second source, naming none: the Rhône partner's own house, Château de Saint Cosme, is wave one's Southern Rhône pick, and Forge Cellars is a separate house. Confirm the label form (Dry Riesling Classique on some listings) and the sites it blends; the single vineyard Rieslings and the Classique Pinot Noir go in others.

picks.why: Cutchogue estate on the North Fork, planted from 1980 by the region record's account, whose Merlot and blends of the Bordeaux grapes set the serious end of the fork; Musée, its blend of those grapes, is the wine of the house.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year and Musée's grapes for the years taught from the house and a second source, and confirm any account of artists' labels before teaching it. The Merlot and the Taste wines go in others. Name no living person.

picks.why: Peconic estate planted in 1978, one of the early vineyards of the North Fork; its long aged Merlot from the old vines is the wine that first set Long Island beside Bordeaux at blind tastings.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the planting year 1978, the release after long ageing and the blind tastings against Bordeaux, with their dates and wines, from the house and a second source, or leave the tastings out. The Old Vines Chardonnay, the Old Vines Cabernet Sauvignon and the sparkling Cuvée go in others. Name no living person.

picks.why: A family estate at Aquebogue on the North Fork since 1983 and one of the few on Long Island to grow Chenin Blanc; its Chenin Blanc is the North Fork white a sommelier is asked about.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the year 1983, the age of the Chenin Blanc vines and the wine's style (dry and unoaked by most accounts) from the house and a second source; the Bordeaux style reds and the Riesling go in others. Say the family, name no living member.

picks.why: The South Fork's landmark at Sagaponack, planted from 1988 by its German born founder; its pale Estate Rosé, made in the Provence manner, became the summer wine of the Hamptons.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the planting from 1988 and the founder's dates (he died in 2008 by recollection) from two sources before naming him. Teach the Estate Rosé, not the Summer in a Bottle range, a separate line; confirm how each is made and where. Christian's Cuvée Merlot goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: A Mattituck estate on the Long Island Sound, planted in 1995 on a family farm and worked with biodynamic methods; Bergen Road, its blend of the Bordeaux grapes, is the house's red to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt between Bergen Road and Alexandra, the house's reserve red by one listing: confirm from the house which it leads with, and the blend for the years taught; the Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc go in others. Confirm the planting year and the biodynamic farming from two sources. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Orange County estate founded in 1976 by a Veneto wine family beside the ruins of a house Thomas Jefferson designed; Octagon, its blend of the Bordeaux grapes named for the house's eight sided room and made only in chosen years, is the Virginia red a sommelier is asked about.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year 1976, the ruins (the house Jefferson designed for James Barbour, burnt in the nineteenth century) and Octagon's name, blend and the years it is made from the house and a second source. Say the Veneto family, name no living member. Its Italian grapes go in others.

picks.why: Orange County estate that led Virginia's turn to Viognier in the early 1990s and brought the native Norton back into commercial use; its Viognier is the white that first made the state's name.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the first Viognier vintage and the competition an early vintage won (1993 by one account) from two sources; the Norton, the Petit Manseng and the Rkatsiteli go in others. Whether the founder is living is not settled here: say the founder, name no one.

picks.why: A Blue Ridge estate in Fauquier County known for wines drawn from its own mountain slopes; the Hardscrabble Chardonnay, from the home vineyard of that name, is the house's white to know, beside a Hardscrabble red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick open between the Hardscrabble Chardonnay and the Hardscrabble red blend: teach the one the house leads with, the other in others. Confirm the founding year and the Hardscrabble site from the house and a second source. Name no living person: say the grower who founded it.

picks.why: A Delaplane estate in the Blue Ridge foothills of northern Virginia making two Bordeaux style reds from its own slopes; Lost Mountain, the Cabernet Sauvignon led one, is the house's flagship.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; not in the region record. Pick in doubt: one source read here gives Lost Mountain to another house. Confirm from the house's own pages that Lost Mountain is its Cabernet Sauvignon led wine and Rendezvous its other, and the first vintage and the site's soils from two sources. Name no living person: say the founder.

picks.why: A northern Virginia estate given to Norton, the native grape raised in Richmond in the 1820s, and to Albariño; its Norton is the state's own red grape in an estate's hands.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label (Locksley Reserve Norton by recollection, not confirmed by any source read here) and which Norton the house leads with, from the house and a second source; the Albariño and the Viognier go in others. Name no living person: say the founder.

picks.why: Molinos estate in the upper Calchaquí, founded in 1831 and one of Argentina's oldest working wineries; Altura Máxima, Malbec from a vineyard at roughly 3,100 metres, puts the altitude of the Calchaquí in one bottle.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 1831 (the library's) and the vineyard's height (roughly 3,100 metres in the region record) from the house and a second source. The Estate Malbec and the Torrontés go in others; teach Altura Máxima as the flagship only if the house presents it so, else ask the merge agent for the Estate Malbec. Ownership is told only as history with its year; name no living person.

picks.why: Cafayate house founded in 1892, the valley's historic cellar, with old vines of Torrontés, Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon; the Old Vines 1945 Torrontés, named for the year its parcel was planted, shows the valley's grape from old vines.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding in 1892 (the region record) and the founders from the house and a second source, and that 1945 is the parcel's planting year. The house was long known by another name by one account: tell the change as history with its year if two sources agree. The red blends and the other Old Vines wines go in others. Present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: A long established Cafayate house, revived in 1938 by the Etchart family and a name for Torrontés in dry and late harvest styles; Arnaldo B., the red named for the man who revived it, is the house's flagship.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The dates 1850 and 1938 and a first vintage of 1990 come from a retailer: confirm from the house and a second source or leave them out, and name Arnaldo Benito Etchart only with his dates. San Pedro de Yacochuya is the family's later estate and a separate house, its own pick. The sale of the house out of the family is history only with its year from two sources. The Torrontés wines go in others.

picks.why: Small estate in the hills above Cafayate at about 2,000 metres, begun in 1988 by the Etchart family with a Bordeaux consultant; Yacochuya is its dense Malbec from old vines, one of Argentina's early wines made for the cellar.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the start (1988) and the first release (1990 by one account), the vineyard's height (6,700 feet by one account) and the vines' age (60 years by one account, over a century by another) from two sources, or leave them out. The consultant is living: say a Bordeaux consultant, never his name. The San Pedro de Yacochuya red and the Torrontés go in others. Bodegas Etchart, of the same family's history, is its own pick.

picks.why: A restored historic family cellar in Cafayate making Torrontés and reds of Malbec and Tannat from the valley's sandy soils; Laborum names its single vineyard wines, its Torrontés the house's white to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt: Laborum is given from recollection and no source read in this roster confirmed it. Confirm from the house that Laborum names its single vineyard wines and which of them it leads with (a Torrontés or a Malbec), else propose a swap. Confirm the cellar's age and the family's tenure from two sources. Name no living person, its consultant included.

picks.why: The Chilecito co-operative of grower families, founded in 1940 and the province's voice in the glass; its Torrontés Riojano, from pergola vines of the Famatina Valley, is the grape named for the province, often under a Fairtrade seal.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year 1940 from the co-operative and a second source. The co-operative bottles Torrontés under several range names (Tilimuqui its organic Fairtrade range by its own site): name the label it leads with and keep Torrontés in the name. Member numbers and volumes are volatile: leave them out. Name no living person, its winemaker included.

picks.why: A modern estate at about 1,700 metres in the Chañarmuyo valley, north of the Famatina, built by a La Rioja family to show what altitude does for the province's grapes; its Malbec is the province's red from height.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt on the wine: no source read in this roster named the house's labels. Confirm from the house which wine it leads with (a Malbec or a Torrontés, and under which range name) and keep the grape in the name, else propose a swap. Confirm the founding year and the vineyard's height from two sources; name no living person, the founder included.

picks.why: A cellar of the Castro Barros valley at Aminga, away from the Famatina, whose Torrontés Riojano is its banner wine; it shows the province's grape from a second valley of the province.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; not in the region record. Confirm the house, its place at Aminga in Castro Barros, its founding year and its Torrontés label from the house and a second source; one directory source alone was read here. Name no living person.

picks.why: San Juan's historic house, founded in the province in 1870 by an Italian immigrant; the Centenario Malbec, a reserve range, is the label by which the old name is met on lists.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding is 1870 by most accounts and 1869 by one: confirm from the house and a second source, and name Santiago Graffigna only with his dates. Confirm the label form (Centenario Reserve Malbec by one listing), its fruit and whether the house leads with it or with its Grand Reserve. A change of ownership in 2019 by one source is history only with two sources; present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: A Tulum Valley house founded in 1993 that carried San Juan Syrah onto export lists; the Gran Syrah, blended from the Tulum, Zonda and Pedernal valleys, is its flagship and the province's grape at full stretch.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year 1993 and the three valleys of the Gran Syrah from the house and a second source. Present ownership is volatile: leave it out. The Reserva range and the Malbec go in others.

picks.why: A San Juan estate built around Syrah, whose warm valley wines made the province's grape familiar abroad; its Syrah is San Juan's warm style in the glass.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt on the wine: no source read in this roster named Callia's leading label. Confirm from the house which Syrah it leads with and keep Syrah in the name, else propose a swap. Sources disagree on whether its fruit is Tulum or Pedernal and on its owner: confirm the vineyards from two sources and leave ownership out. Callia and Pyros belong to one group by one account: teach them as two houses only if each keeps its own cellar and vineyards.

picks.why: A Pedernal Valley estate at about 1,400 metres on the province's high western side, showing what altitude does for San Juan Malbec and Syrah; the Vineyard Block No. 4 Malbec, from one block of the estate, is its wine to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label form (Vineyard Block No. 4 on one review listing, printed with the numero sign), the block's height and soils and the house's founding year from the house and a second source; the Appellation Malbec and Syrah go in others. See Callia's note on the group both belong to by one account.

picks.why: A small project at Barreal in the Calingasta Valley, bottling old pergola Criolla and other heritage grapes from smallholders' vineyards under the Andes; its Criolla is the old mission grape of the Spanish made as a light, fresh red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label (Cara Sur Criolla, or Criolla Chica by name) and which Criolla it is, from the house and a second source; the house's name is said to be a mountain face: confirm which before teaching it. One founding partner is of the family of Familia Zuccardi, wave one's Mendoza pick: Cara Sur is a separate project, and none of its founders is named, all being living. The Bonarda and the Moscatel go in others.

picks.why: Mainque estate in the Río Negro founded in 2004 around abandoned own rooted Pinot Noir and farmed biodynamically; Treinta y Dos, from the vines planted in 1932 and named for the year, showed that Argentina had more than Malbec to give.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 2004, the parcel's planting year 1932 and the biodynamic farming from the house and a second source. Cincuenta y Cinco and Barda go in others. The founder is of the family behind Tenuta San Guido, wave one's Bolgheri pick: Chacra is a separate house; say the family, name no living member.

picks.why: The historic Alto Valle house at General Roca, making wine since the early twentieth century; its Old Vineyard Sémillon, from the estate's old vines, is the Patagonian white a sommelier is asked about.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding is given as 1909 and as 1914 by different sources: confirm from the house and a second source or leave it empty, and name the founder only with his dates. Confirm the label (Old Vineyard Sémillon, or Old Vine Sémillon on later releases) and the vines' planting years. The Gran Reserva Malbec, the Pinot Noir and the Estate 1909 Merlot go in others.

picks.why: A Río Negro estate built on an old own rooted Malbec parcel of the Alto Valle; Noemía, from that parcel, is the house's flagship and the wine that showed Patagonian Malbec of fine bones.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the place (Valle Azul by recollection), the parcel's planting year (1932 by recollection), the first vintage and the founding from the house and a second source; the founders are living: say the founders. A Lisa and J. Alberto go in others.

picks.why: A San Patricio del Chañar estate in Neuquén, whose cellar works uncovered a dinosaur fossil remembered in its Saurus range; the Saurus Pinot Noir is the range's red a guest meets on lists.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year, the fossil (its kind and the year found) and the Saurus label from the house and a second source. Pick open between the Saurus Pinot Noir and the house's Malbec: teach the one the house leads with; the Familia Schroeder upper range goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The pioneering estate of San Patricio del Chañar, which planted the Neuquén desert for wine and is known for Malbec, Merlot and Pinot Noir; its Special Blend is the house's flagship red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year (the late 1990s by recollection), the Special Blend's grapes and its label form (Special Blend Reserva del Fin del Mundo by recollection) from the house and a second source. Present ownership is volatile. Name no living person.

picks.why: Founded at Vicuña in 1998, the estate that proved the Elqui could make fine Syrah and Sauvignon Blanc and not pisco alone; its Syrah is the north's red to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick open on the label: the house bottles Syrah in several ranges (Reserva, Gran Reserva, and Titón from a site nearer the sea by one account); confirm from the house which leads and how it is made, and keep Syrah in the name. Confirm the founding year 1998 and the founders from two sources; name no living person. Mayu, the family's other Elqui label, goes in others.

picks.why: Among the highest vineyards of Chile, above 2,000 metres in the upper Elqui at Alcohuaz, with grapes trodden by foot and pressed by hand; Tococo, its Syrah, is the north's mountain red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick open between Tococo (named as its Syrah on one listing) and Rhu (the house's blend by recollection, not confirmed): confirm from the house which it leads with, the grapes of each and the vineyards' heights. Confirm the founding year and the family from two sources; name no living person.

picks.why: The Limarí house near Ovalle whose Talinay vineyard, on limestone near the Pacific, defined the valley's taut, saline Chardonnay; the Talinay Chardonnay is the wine of that site.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year, the Talinay vineyard's distance from the sea and its limestone from the house and a second source (the house's own page names Talinay its range from the site); the Talinay Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc and the house's Syrah go in others. Name no living person; present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: A Maipo house founded in 1885 at Talagante, here for its Limarí wine: the T.H. Chardonnay of its Terroir Hunter range, from Quebrada Seca in the west of the valley, shows a large house reading the valley's limestone.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house's home is the Maipo; it stands here for its Limarí bottling, as the region holds few houses of its own whose wines this roster could confirm. Confirm the founding (1885 at Talagante by recollection) and the label form (T.H. Chardonnay, Limarí, from Quebrada Seca by the listings read here) from the house and a second source; its Maipo wines go in others. Present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: Founded at Panquehue in 1870, the historic house of the Aconcagua valley; Don Maximiano Founder's Reserve, its Cabernet Sauvignon led blend named for the founder, is the house's flagship and the valley's red to know.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 1870 (the library's) and the founder's dates from two sources before naming him. Confirm Don Maximiano's blend and first vintage from the house. Seña (w-sena), the family's own Aconcagua blend begun with a Napa partner, is a separate estate and a wine record of the library: it goes in this record's others or traps, never as a second pick of the family, and the family's Maipo estate is already wave one's pick. The Las Pizarras wines go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Estate founded in 2000 at Lo Abarca in the San Antonio Valley, four kilometres from the Pacific, which took Chilean Sauvignon Blanc to the edge of the ocean; the Cipreses Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc is its single vineyard wine to know.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 2000, the distance from the sea and the Cipreses site from the house and a second source; the Lo Abarca Hills Syrah and the Miramar Vineyard Riesling go in others. The founder is living: say the founder, never her name.

picks.why: Founded in 1997, the house that brought Maipo river water to the Leyda hills and planted the zone that bears its name; the Lot 21 Pinot Noir, from a single lot of its vineyards, is the zone's red to know, beside its Sauvignon Blanc.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year 1997 and the pipeline from the Maipo river from the house and a second source. Pick open between the Lot 21 Pinot Noir and the Garuma Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc, both single vineyard wines on the listings read here: teach the one the house leads with, the other in others; Casa Marín already teaches the zone's Sauvignon Blanc in this group. Present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: A biodynamic estate in the Rosario valley between Casablanca and San Antonio, whose EQ Syrah showed that cool coastal Chile could make peppery reds in the northern Rhône manner.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year, the biodynamic farming and the Rosario valley's place under the appellations (San Antonio by most accounts) from the house and a second source; the EQ Pinot Noir, the EQ Sauvignon Blanc and the Corralillo range go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: A Casablanca estate in the western hills of the valley, planted on the family's ranch and known for Pinot Noir and cool Syrah; the Tobiano Pinot Noir is its Casablanca red to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt for the group's Casablanca place: Casas del Bosque and Veramonte are larger houses of the valley, and the merge agent may prefer one of them with a Sauvignon Blanc. Confirm the planting year and Tobiano's sites from the house and a second source; the house's Sauvignon Blanc and Syrah go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Penedès family's Chilean house, at Curicó since 1979, which brought stainless steel to the country's cellars; Manso de Velasco, first made in 1985 from old Cabernet Sauvignon vines and named for the founder of Curicó, was its first premium wine.
picks.note: Not joined: p-torres is the Familia Torres record, the Spain lane's Penedès pick (Mas La Plana), and Miguel Torres Chile is the family's separate Chilean company, to be said so in the record. Its own page, read in summary, gives 1985 and the city's founding by José Manso de Velasco in 1743: confirm the vines' age and site from a second source. The Cordillera Carignan, the Escaleras de Empedrado Pinot Noir and the Santa Digna range go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Founded at Lontué in 1879 as Champagne Valdivieso, the country's historic sparkling house; Caballo Loco, a multi vintage red blended in the manner of a solera and numbered by release, is the house's wine a sommelier is asked about.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding year 1879 and the solera manner come from one secondary source and the region record: confirm from the house and a second source, and how Caballo Loco is numbered and blended. The founder may be named only with his dates from two sources. The sparkling wines go in others.

picks.why: A Maule family house of French origin at Mingre in the dry farmed secano and a leader of the País revival; País Salvaje comes from wild vines that climb into the trees and is fermented with native yeasts.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house also labels as J. Bouchon: confirm the name it uses, the family's arrival and founding years and the place at Mingre from the house and a second source. The white País Salvaje and the País Viejo go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: A small house making wines from tiny parcels of smallholders in the Maule and Itata, and a member of VIGNO; its Truquilemu Carignan, from old dry farmed bush vines of the Maule secano, is the Carignan revival in one bottle.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; not in the region record. Confirm the label form (Cru Truquilemu Carignan on one listing, and its VIGNO bottling from the same vineyard by another), the vineyard's place and the founding year from the house and a second source; the house's other Maule and Itata wines go in others. Name no living person: say the founders.

picks.why: A house of a Norwegian shipping family, farmed organically, with old dry farmed Carignan at Cauquenes in the Maule secano; its Orzada Carignan is that Maule Carignan in the house's hands.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house's winery stands in the Maipo by recollection: confirm, and teach it here for its Cauquenes Carignan only. Confirm the founding year, the Cauquenes vineyard and the Orzada label from the house and a second source; the house's other wines, its VIGNO bottling among them, go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Isla de Maipo house founded in 1934 whose old vine Cinsault and País from Itata, fermented and aged in old clay tinajas, led the south's revival on export lists; the Viejas Tinajas Cinsault is that wine.
picks.note: The house's home is the Maipo; it stands here for its Itata wines, as the region record names it. Confirm the founding year 1934 (the library's), the vineyard's place in Itata and the age of the tinajas from the house and a second source; Gallardía del Itata and the Maipo wines go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: An Itata project built on smallholders' dry farmed bush vines, bottling old vine Cinsault, País and Moscatel at low alcohol; the Grand Itata Tinto, mostly Cinsault with a little País, is the dry granite hills of Itata in a glass.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year, the blend and the vines' age from the house and a second source, teaching no yearly percentage; the Grand Itata Blanco goes in others. One of its two founders also makes A Los Viñateros Bravos, left out so the group holds no two houses of one maker. Name no living person: say the founders.

picks.why: A Maipo house founded with Bordeaux partners, here for its far southern wine: the Sol de Sol Chardonnay, from vines first planted in 1993 at Traiguén in the Malleco and first released in 2000, opened Chile's far south to fine wine.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house's winery is in the Maipo; it stands here for Sol de Sol, from the Malleco, which the region record counts with Itata and Bío Bío. Confirm the planting in 1993 and the first release in 2000 (from the importer's page) and the Bordeaux partners from two sources; the founder who planted the vines is living: say a Chilean agronomist, never his name. The Sol de Sol Pinot Noir and the Maipo wines go in others.

picks.why: A family cellar at Yumbel in the Bío Bío with vines said to go back to the eighteenth century, known for traditional pipeño, the light, rustic País of the southern countryside; its Pipeño is that old country wine bottled for lists.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the family's tenure and the vines' age (the eighteenth century by the region record, a claim to hedge), the place at Yumbel (Secano Interior de Yumbel on one listing) and the Pipeño's grape and making from the house and a second source; its other País and Moscatel wines go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: A natural wine grower of Concepción working old País and Moscatel vines in the Bío Bío and Itata near the Nahuelbuta range; Rivera del Notro, red País from the Bío Bío, is the old mission grape made in the manner of the new south.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; not in the region record. A house keeps its name, here the grower's own: the grower is living, so the record names the house and says no more of the person than the grower. Rivera del Notro names both a red País from the Bío Bío and a white blend from Itata: teach the red, and put the white in others. Confirm the founding year and the vineyards' places from the house and a second source.
